name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.absoluteMaximizer_satellites_almost_norm
title: One fixed satellite family almost norms every detected unit vector

content.display_title: One fixed satellite family almost norms every detected unit vector
content.one_sentence_role: Uses a detecting coefficient and its matching satellite without replacing the family.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. Let $p:V\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in V).$$
Thus $p$ is a norm. We use $p$ for the model distance and $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ for reference-coordinate estimates; the two norms are allowed to coincide. A $p$-dual contraction is a continuous real linear functional $r$ satisfying $|r(x)|\le p(x)$ for every $x$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard coordinate vectors. For an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals on $V$, put
$$M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j},\quad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_Fx,\quad
\mathcal U_p=\{F:\forall i,x,\ |\ell_i(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For a real number $\eta$, define the attained maximum and near-maximal set by
$$D_p=\max_{F\in\mathcal U_p}|\det M_F|>0,\qquad
\mathcal N_{p,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U_p:D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
Admissibility is measured with $p$; the matrices are written in the fixed reference coordinates.

Let $J$ be a finite index set, possibly empty; choose coefficients $c_a\in V$ for $a\in J$. A configuration is a pair $Q=(F,s)$, where $F$ is a frame and $s=(s_a)_{a\in J}$ is a family of additional continuous real linear functionals, called satellites. Write
$$\Omega_p^J=\{(F,s):F\in\mathcal U_p,\ \forall a,x,\ |s_a(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For any real weight $w$, let $M_F[i\leftarrow r]$ replace row $i$ by $(r(e_j))_j$ and set
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
An absolute maximizer means a single $Q\in\Omega_p^J$ with $|\Phi_{w,c}(Q')|\le|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|$ for every $Q'\in\Omega_p^J$. It need not maximize the signed polynomial.

A common inverse bound consists of a number $K>0$ and the uniform estimate
$$p(M_F^{-1}c)\le K\|c\|_\infty\qquad(F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta},\ c\in V).$$
It is fixed independently of the particular frame and coefficient. When $\eta<D_p$, every such frame has nonzero determinant. Suppose $\eta<D_p$, $Q=(F,s)$ is an admissible absolute maximizer with $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$, and a real $\rho$ satisfies the coefficient-detection hypothesis
$$\forall F^\prime\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}\ \forall x^\prime\in V\ (p(x^\prime)=1),\quad
\exists a\in J,\ p(x^\prime-M_{F^\prime}^{-1}c_a)\le K\rho.$$
Then, for any $x$ with $p(x)=1$, there is $a\in J$ with $1-2K\rho\le|s_a(x)|$.
content.assumptions: A fixed common inverse bound $K>0$ with its uniform estimate, a fixed coefficient family, the full detection hypothesis, the positive determinant gap, admissibility, near-maximality and absolute maximality are required. There is no separate positivity assumption on $\rho$ or $w$.
content.conclusion: The index may depend on $x$, but the entire satellite family $s$ and its maximizing configuration have already been fixed. The output evaluates the satellite having the same index as the detected coefficient.
content.proof_summary: Detect one coefficient near the given unit vector, use its matching norming satellite, then apply the two-error estimate.

proof_steps.text:
**Choose the index from the supplied detection hypothesis.** Apply that hypothesis to the actual near-maximal base $F$ and the given unit vector $x$. It yields one $a\in J$ and, with $z_a=M_F^{-1}c_a$,
   $$p(x-z_a)\le K\rho.$$
   This is a hypothesis about all near-maximal frames, not a property inferred merely from the name of a coefficient family.

**Use the matching satellite, without changing the family.** For the index $a$ just selected,
   $$|s_a(y)|\le p(y)\ (y\in V),\qquad |s_a(z_a)|=p(z_a),\qquad p(x-z_a)\le K\rho.$$
   The first is admissibility. The middle equality is [absolute norm attainment at coefficient preimages](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L897-L950) applied to the same $\eta,Q,c,w,a$, using the determinant gap, admissibility, near-maximality and absolute maximality. The last inequality is Step 1. Together with $p(x)=1$, they give the complete calculation
   $$1-K\rho\le p(z_a)=|s_a(z_a)|
   \le |s_a(x)|+p(z_a-x)\le |s_a(x)|+K\rho.$$
   This is [the nearby norming-point estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L970-L990) applied to the same functional $s_a$, the points $x$ and $z_a$, and the error bound $K\rho$. Rearranging yields $1-2K\rho\le |s_a(x)|$. No new Hahn--Banach functional replaces the already fixed $s_a$.

content.lean_realization_notes: The full quantifier order is defined in [coefficient detection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L953-L958). An actual finite net supplies it as follows. For a near-maximal $F^\prime$ and unit $x^\prime$, [contractive frame coordinates](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L349-L354) gives $\|T_{F^\prime}x^\prime\|_\infty\le1$, while the uniform inverse estimate gives $1\le K\|T_{F^\prime}x^\prime\|_\infty$. Thus [membership in the coefficient annulus](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L357-L378) puts $T_{F^\prime}x^\prime$ in $\{c:1/K\le\|c\|_\infty\le1\}$. A center within reference distance $\rho$ then gives, by [inverse transport of the coefficient error](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L381-L394), $p(x^\prime-M_{F^\prime}^{-1}c_a)\le K\rho$. This is [a close preimage from the finite net](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L406-L424). The present theorem assumes detection explicitly and does not itself select that net.
